destination.name: Lord Howe Island
destination.tagline: A crescent-shaped volcanic island in the Tasman Sea with a coral lagoon, steep walks and a cap on visitors.
destination.description: Lord Howe Island lies 600 km east of Port Macquarie and is about 10 km long, the remnant of a volcano. It was World Heritage listed in 1982 and only 400 tourists are allowed on it at any one time. Ned's Beach, with fish to hand-feed and snorkelling over reef, sits on the sheltered lagoon side, while surf beaches face west. Ball's Pyramid, a sea stack 23 km south-east, draws divers.

goodToKnow.title: Flights are limited
goodToKnow.detail: QantasLink flies daily from Sydney in about two hours, fares run about $1,000 to $1,200 return, and seats must be booked with your accommodation; bad weather can turn flights back.

goodToKnow.title: Mount Gower needs a guide
goodToKnow.detail: The 8-hour Mount Gower trek is guided only, about $200, with rope-assisted climbs, and the Mount Eliza track to North Bay is closed from 1 September to 1 March.

goodToKnow.title: Bikes, cash and booking
goodToKnow.detail: There are no taxis or public transport, so cycling is the main way to get around, only Australian currency is accepted, and restaurants usually need booking before noon.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: Visit in {months}: Wikivoyage calls summer the island's best weather, and red-tailed tropicbirds court over Malabar Hill from September to May.
